newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Brazil may extend exceptions on import limits.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may extend exceptions on import limits.

text.p: Brazil may decide to extend the exceptions granted to its Mercosur partners on the import financing restrictions the country introduced in March, a Brazilian government official said Wednesday.

"The possibility that the exceptions will be extended exists," Arnolfo Carvalho, the spokesman for Brazil's Finance Minister Pedro Malan, told journalists at a Mercosur meeting in Asuncion. "We have asked every country to evaluate the trade impact of the measure and the conclusion of minister (Pedro) Malan is that it has not had a repercussion on trade flows in the Mercosur."
Brazil agreed to ease the restrictions on import financing of less than a year for the Mercosur after protests from fellow members Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.
Brazil originally agreed to ease the rules until July. Carvalho did not say for how long the extension could be.
The dispute has been a key issue at this week's Mercosur summit, which concludes Thursday with a meeting of presidents from the customs union.
On Wednesday, Argentine officials suggested a new special regime for Mercosur imports could be introduced by Brazil.
Economy ministers from the four countries were expected to hold a press conference later Wednesday.
